outputs.L1: A FinFET device is provided. The FinFET device includes a substrate having at least one fin, a gate stack, a spacer, a strained layer, a composite etch-stop layer, a dielectric layer, and a connector. The gate stack extends across the at least one fin, and the spacer is disposed on a sidewall of the gate stack. The strained layer is formed in the substrate adjacent to the gate stack. The composite etch-stop layer is disposed on the spacer and the strained layer, and is thicker on the spacer than on the strained layer. The dielectric layer is disposed on the composite etch-stop layer. The connector is positioned over and electrically connected to the strained layer. A first upper portion of a first sidewall of the connector contacts the composite etch-stop layer, while a second upper portion of a second sidewall of the connector is separated from the composite etch-stop layer by the dielectric layer disposed therebetween.
outputs.L2: A FinFET device includes a substrate with at least one fin, a gate stack extending across the fin, and a spacer disposed along a sidewall of the gate stack. A strained layer is formed in the substrate adjacent to the gate stack. A composite etch-stop layer covers both the spacer and the strained layer, with a greater thickness over the spacer than over the strained layer. A dielectric layer overlies the composite etch-stop layer. The device further includes a connector positioned above and electrically coupled to the strained layer. An upper section of a first connector sidewall directly contacts the composite etch-stop layer, while an upper section of a second connector sidewall is spaced apart from the composite etch-stop layer by an intervening portion of the dielectric layer.
outputs.L3:
The FinFET device includes a substrate having at least one fin, a gate stack, a spacer, a strained layer, a composite etching stop layer, a dielectric layer, and a connector. The gate stack extends across the fin, while the spacer is disposed along a sidewall of the gate stack. The strained layer is formed in the substrate adjacent to the gate stack.

The composite etching stop layer covers both the spacer and the strained layer. Its thickness over the spacer is greater than its thickness over the strained layer. The dielectric layer is disposed over the composite etching stop layer. The connector extends through the dielectric layer and is electrically connected to the strained layer. A first upper sidewall portion of the connector directly contacts the composite etching stop layer, whereas a second upper sidewall portion is separated from the composite etching stop layer by the dielectric layer.
outputs.L4:
A semiconductor device includes a FinFET formed on a substrate and having a fin structure, a gate structure crossing the fin structure, gate spacers disposed along opposite sidewalls of the gate structure, and a strained semiconductor layer adjacent to the gate structure. A composite contact-etching stop layer is formed over the FinFET. The composite layer has a relatively large thickness on the gate spacers and a smaller thickness over the strained semiconductor layer. This nonuniform thickness provides enhanced protection for the gate structure while allowing an electrical contact to be formed through the overlying materials with a controlled etching depth.

A dielectric layer is disposed over the composite contact-etching stop layer. An opening extends through the dielectric layer toward the strained semiconductor layer, and an electrically conductive connector is formed in the opening to establish electrical connection with the underlying source/drain region. Due to the shape and position of the opening, the connector has an asymmetric relationship with the composite contact-etching stop layer. On one upper sidewall of the connector, the conductive material directly contacts the etching stop layer. On the opposite upper sidewall, a portion of the dielectric layer remains between the connector and the etching stop layer, electrically and physically separating them.

The thicker portion of the etching stop layer on the gate spacer increases the process margin during formation of the connector and reduces the likelihood that contact etching will damage the gate spacer or expose the gate electrode. At the same time, the thinner portion over the strained semiconductor layer facilitates removal of the stop layer at the intended contact location, thereby reducing over-etching and improving electrical coupling to the source/drain region. The asymmetric connector configuration further accommodates alignment variations while preserving dielectric isolation on the protected side. Together, these features enable reliable contact formation, limit unintended short circuits, protect nearby gate structures, and improve the performance and manufacturing yield of the FinFET device.
outputs.L5: The FinFET transistor has transformed modern semiconductor design by improving performance and reducing power leakage. Provided that manufacturers maintain precise fabrication processes, FinFET technology enables smaller, faster, and more energy-efficient electronic devices.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract describing a FinFET device with a fin, gate stack, spacer, strained layer, composite etching stop layer of varying thickness, dielectric layer, and asymmetrically positioned connector.
counterfactuals.output: A semiconductor device includes a fin extending from a substrate and a gate stack disposed over and across the fin. A gate spacer is positioned along a sidewall of the gate stack, and a strained semiconductor layer is disposed on a source/drain region of the fin adjacent to the gate spacer. A composite etching stop layer extends over the strained semiconductor layer and along the gate spacer, the composite etching stop layer having portions of different thicknesses. A dielectric layer is disposed over the composite etching stop layer. A conductive connector extends through the dielectric layer and the composite etching stop layer to electrically contact the strained semiconductor layer. The conductive connector is asymmetrically positioned relative to the strained semiconductor layer and has a centerline laterally offset from a centerline of the strained semiconductor layer. The varying thickness of the composite etching stop layer facilitates formation and alignment of the conductive connector while protecting adjacent device structures.

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize a semiconductor device invention in one paragraph, emphasizing that the composite etch-stop layer is thicker over the gate spacer than over the strained source/drain layer.
counterfactuals.output: The invention relates to a semiconductor device featuring a gate structure with sidewall spacers, strained source/drain regions, and a composite etch-stop layer engineered with nonuniform thickness. In particular, the composite etch-stop layer is thicker over the gate spacer than over the strained source/drain layer, providing enhanced protection and etch control near the gate while limiting stress relaxation or excessive material buildup above the source/drain regions. This configuration supports accurate contact formation, preserves strain-induced carrier-mobility improvements, and enables improved device performance and manufacturing reliability.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a formal technical description of a FinFET structure in which a connector contacts a strained layer, with one upper connector sidewall touching the composite etching stop layer and the opposite sidewall separated from it by a dielectric.
counterfactuals.output:
A FinFET structure includes a semiconductor fin extending from a substrate, a gate structure disposed over a channel region of the fin, and a strained semiconductor layer disposed adjacent to the gate structure in a source/drain region. A composite etching stop layer, comprising a plurality of etch-stop sublayers, extends over at least a portion of the strained semiconductor layer. A dielectric layer is disposed over the composite etching stop layer.

A conductive connector extends through the dielectric layer and the composite etching stop layer to electrically contact the strained semiconductor layer. An upper portion of the conductive connector has first and second opposing sidewalls. The first sidewall directly contacts the composite etching stop layer, whereas the second sidewall is spaced apart from the composite etching stop layer by an intervening portion of the dielectric layer. Accordingly, the composite etching stop layer and the dielectric layer have an asymmetric lateral arrangement relative to the upper portion of the connector.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a concise semiconductor patent abstract for a FinFET having a nonuniform composite etch-stop layer and an asymmetric contact configuration above a strained source/drain region.
counterfactuals.output: A semiconductor device includes a FinFET having a fin, a gate structure over a channel region of the fin, and a strained source/drain region adjacent to the gate structure. A composite etch-stop layer overlies the strained source/drain region and includes first and second dielectric materials having different etch characteristics.
